business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Jurisdictional Commercial Arbitration and Asset Tracing

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (European continental tradition, with constitutional review and substantial commercial arbitration legislation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement, in force 15 May 2012
Colombia–European Union Trade Agreement, in force 2013
Colombia–United Kingdom Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments, signed 17 March 2010
Colombia–Spain Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, in force 21 August 1997
Colombia–Chile Free Trade Agreement and Pacific Alliance Additional Protocol
Colombia–Peru and Colombia–Mexico Pacific Alliance trade integration instruments
Colombia–United States Double Taxation Convention, in force 1 January 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (creation of UIAF); Law 1121 of 2006 (financing of terrorism); Law 1258 of 2008 (SAS regime); Law 2155 of 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUB); Decree 2199 of 2022 (UBO registration and information transmission rules); Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia External Circular 007 of 2014, as amended, including Title V Chapter XI and SAGRILAFT provisions on UBO identification and enhanced due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague countries, Colombian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate UBO declaration certificate of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country corporate registry, competent AML authority, or independent auditor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Colombian legal representative / incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of signing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and traceable source of funds confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating financial institution holding the funding account of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport or national identity document of each direct shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or civil registry of the individual's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified notarial copy; apostilled or consular legalized if a certified public registration copy is demanded

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of criminal record / judicial good conduct for the proposed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the representative's current country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, beneficial owners, and material funding counterparties against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council sanctions consolidations, EU Financial Sanctions Database, Colombian UIAF terrorism-financing lists, Colombian Procuraduría disciplinary records, and the RUB screening schema. PEPs require enhanced due diligence, additional documentary evidence of legitimate source of funds, and senior management approval prior to incorporation; negative news and adverse registry checks are mandatory for all foreign entities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cámara de Comercio / Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES), principally through the Cámara de Comercio of Bogotá or the competent local chamber for the registered office domicile
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be expressed in Spanish using Latin-script characters; foreign-language words must be transliterated into Spanish and must not mislead as to the corporate form, industry, or public nature of the entity. Names may include initials, ablations, and numbers if the result is distinguishable in the RUES homonym registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations issued by the Cámara de Comercio are valid for 30 calendar days and are not extendable; upon expiry a new reservation may be filed. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a reconsideration request with the same Cámara de Comercio within five working days under Article 8 of Law 1437 of 2011. If the chamber maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an appeal (recurso de apelación) with the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within ten working days. A different, revised name may be simultaneously reserved at any time without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible only as an administrative correspondence address, not as the sole commercial substance of a cross-border litigation chamber under ISIC 6910. The SAS must maintain a physical infrastructure, client files, trust-account records, and responsible legal personnel at or through a verifiable Colombian establishment; use of a virtual-only address significantly increases regulatory, tax, and beneficial-ownership scrutiny and may be rejected by DIAN, UIAF, or the Cámara de Comercio for substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15%-25% annual risk for a low-risk SAS engaged in commercial litigation if a physical office with proper records is maintained. The likelihood rises to 30%-40% if a purely virtual or shared coworking address is declared, if UBO information is incomplete or inconsistent, or if PEP/sanction matches appear during screening; unannounced on-site inspections may be conducted by UIAF, DIAN, or the competent Superintendencia as part of AML/CFT and administrative substance review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation, homonym search, and SAS registration before the Cámara de Comercio
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office domicile
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory chamber tariff based on zero or minimum declared share capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and private-document execution of the SAS incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary fee schedule based on the certified public deed or private document value

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate and individual documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the document's country of origin and, if required, Colombian consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official government fees of the apostille authority plus consular legalization tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of apostilled or consularized foreign documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Official certified translator in Colombia (traductor oficial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per source document and per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT screening and PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and UIAF database checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance data provider retained by the responsible law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per shareholder and per ultimate beneficial owner screened

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, UBO piercing analysis, and incorporation coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark flat fee for Stage 1 work on a low-risk SAS with cross-border litigation scope

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 1, 3-5, 11, 12, 16, and 46; Código de Comercio, Articles 110-119, 129-131, and 142.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Registro Mercantil), with subsequent registration before the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) for tax purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Private Instrument of Incorporation) registered before the Chamber of Commerce; a notarial Escritura Pública is required if real property or specialized in-kind contributions are part of the share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-up capital is required by Law 1258 of 2008. Shareholders determine the capital amount in the bylaws. If contributions are in cash, funds must be received and acknowledged by the legal representative; no escrow account is mandatory, but unpaid subscribed capital must be fully paid within two years from incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] S.A.S. Adopted unanimously by written consent of the shareholders on [Date]. WHEREAS the incorporators have subscribed the entire authorized share capital and approved the bylaws. RESOLVED: 1. The subscription of [NUMBER] shares, with payment terms under Article 8 of the bylaws, is ratified. 2. The registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], municipality of [CITY], and shall be used for all statutory correspondence. 3. [NAME] is appointed Legal Representative/Manager and [NAME] is appointed Secretary, who are jointly authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete registration filings. 4. Management is instructed to register the company with the Chamber of Commerce, DIAN, and relevant professional licensing bodies before commencing any legal or litigation operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Homonymy Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, online via the Registro Único Empresarial (www.rue.com.co) or in person at the local Chamber.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two or more proposed corporate names in Spanish to the Chamber's business-name search module. The system will indicate whether the name is identical, similar, or unavailable. Once an available name is identified, request the Certificate of Homonymy, which reserves the name for the registering party for a limited statutory period, usually 30 business days.
required_dossiers: Completed name-search application form
Valid identification document or passport of the incorporator
Power of attorney if the application is submitted by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected because it is identical or confusingly similar to an existing trade name, select a new distinctive name or modify the corporate object descriptors and re-submit. A written reconsideration request may also be filed before the Chamber in accordance with the Código de Procedimiento Administrativo, Articles 74-76.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Private Incorporation Instrument and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders' assembly in private document; notary public only when assets contributed require a public deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Private Instrument of Incorporation, including the full bylaws, share subscription, registered office, corporate purpose, representation and management provisions, duration, and internal governance rules. Sign the document before a notary when required, and have all shareholder signatures authenticated. The instrument must state that the subscribed capital has been paid as agreed in the bylaws.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation document and bylaws
Certificate of Homonymy issued by the Chamber of Commerce
Share subscription schedule and capital payment plan
Identification documents of all shareholders and initial officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary or reviewer identifies errors, amend the draft, have all shareholders initial the revisions, and re-execute the document. If the document was notarized, a corrective amendment must be executed in the same form before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Mercantile Registry and Issuance of the Matrícula Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the jurisdiction where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation instrument to the Chamber's Mercantile Registry window or its online portal. Complete the official registration form, declare the amount of capital, and pay the registration tariff and registration tax. The Chamber verifies the legal formalities, enters the company into the mercantile registry, and issues the Matrícula Mercantil and the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation.
required_dossiers: Executed incorporation instrument and bylaws
Certificate of Homonymy
Completed Chamber registration form
Proof of payment of the registration tariff and tax
Identification documents of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues an objection or requirement, correct the specified information or provide the requested clarifications within the granted period, generally 10 business days. If the registration is denied, an administrative reconsideration or appeal under the Código de Procedimiento Administrativo may be filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with DIAN – RUT and NIT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (delegated to authorized bank and Chamber points of attention).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After mercantile registration, apply for the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) through the DIAN electronic portal or authorized service point. Submit the data required to obtain the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT), including the certificate of existence, economic activity codes according to ISIC, address, legal representative information, and the company's main compliance profile. After approval, download the RUT certificate and register the legal representative's digital signature for electronic invoicing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation issued by the Chamber of Commerce
Executed incorporation instrument
Valid identification of the legal representative and shareholders
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or suspends the RUT application, correct the inconsistencies identified in the rejection notice and resubmit. If the rejection is based on substantive legal interpretation, an appeal may be filed before DIAN within applicable statutory deadlines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Foreign Investment Registration (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Colombian credit institution (bank) and Banco de la República through the local intermediary for foreign exchange declaration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name by supplying the Chamber certificate, RUT, incorporation instrument, and legal representative identification. If a non-resident shareholder makes a capital contribution or subscribes shares, the contribution must be channeled through the local exchange market and reported on the applicable foreign exchange declaration form before the Banco de la República, preserving funds to support the entity's registered capital.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
RUT
Incorporation document and bylaws
Legal representative identification
Know-your-client and AML forms required by the bank
Foreign investment declaration form if capital is transferred from abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence documents, provide them promptly or select an alternative authorized institution. If the foreign exchange declaration is rejected, correct and resubmit the form through the same bank; late submission may trigger fines, so administrative regularization with DIAN and the Banco de la República should be initiated without delay.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejo Superior de la Judicatura – Unidad de Registro Nacional de Abogados (URNA) for professional legal authorization, together with the municipal Secretaría de Gobierno or competent planning authority for the commercial establishment operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Tarjeta Profesional de Abogado and Licencia de Funcionamiento de Establecimiento Comercial de Servicios Profesionales

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for national-level environmental licensing; Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente or the local environmental authority for municipal-level environmental compliance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment; a professional office engaged in cross-border commercial litigation and asset tracing is classified as a Category 3 low-impact service establishment under applicable environmental regulations, requiring only compliance with environmental registration and waste management duties if any.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with municipal water supply and sewerage standards, and with Resolución No. 0631 de 2015 for domestic wastewater parameters if office operations generate discharges. Hazardous or special waste (batteries, electronic equipment, toners) must be handled under Decree 4741 de 2005 and returned to authorized reverse-logistics channels. No industrial atmospheric emissions or VOC thresholds apply to the office-based activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before commencing operations, the premises must obtain a fire-safety certificate from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos, verify structural load-bearing conditions through an engineer's certificate for office occupancy, and comply with workplace safety and health obligations under Resolución 0312 de 2019, including evacuation plans, emergency brigades, and registration with a licensed Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); transactional portal: MUISCA via www.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must (1) appoint a Colombian legal representative or attorney-in-fact; (2) obtain or update the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) by filing the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) before DIAN; (3) register the precise economic activities, responsible VAT status, and e-invoicing class; (4) maintain the RUT data in force for all customs, foreign-exchange and tax filings. The Colombian S.A.S. itself must complete the same RUT/NIT procedure upon incorporation before starting taxable operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Colombian tax law. A qualifying small taxpayer may elect the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE), which replaces income tax, national consumption tax, and VAT in a unified regime, subject to gross-income ceilings and excluded activities; otherwise the S.A.S. remains an ordinary income-tax taxpayer at entity level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre las Ventas - IVA) with supplementary national consumption taxes on designated services and digital supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general COP threshold: VAT registration through RUT is compulsory before engaging in taxable supplies. For the optional SIMPLE regime, the prior-year gross ordinary income ceiling is approximately COP 3,765,000,000 (80,000 UVT for 2024); taxpayers above that ceiling must remain in the ordinary VAT/income regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-responsible taxpayers must use DIAN-registered invoicing software or API connectors, transmit electronic invoices in XML/UBL format to DIAN's validation service, obtain and embed the unique generation code (CUFE/CUNE) and QR, and report invoice events including acceptation, rejection and credit/debit notes. Transmission is required in near-real-time before the invoice is considered valid for VAT and customs purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for 0% VAT when the customs export declaration is lodged and the goods physically leave Colombian customs territory. Services qualify as 'exported services' when rendered in Colombia but economically used or exploited abroad for the direct benefit of a foreign beneficiary and payment is received from a non-Colombian source; the supporting evidence must be available before claiming the zero rate on the VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / multimodal transport document
Commercial invoice and packing list matched to the DEX
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Canalización / Reintegro de Divisas) issued by an authorized Colombian foreign-exchange intermediary
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN cross-checks zero-rated export sales against customs (DEX), banking (foreign-exchange channeling) and VAT-return databases. If the zero rate is applied without substantiated export documentation or timely FX repatriation, DIAN may reclassify the revenue as taxable domestic supply and assess 19% IVA, plus default interest, price-level adjustment, and an inaccuracy penalty that can approximate 100-200% of the tax omitted. Intentional document falsification or reliance on shell foreign beneficiaries is criminally punishable and triggers retrospective clawback of VAT refunds under the statutory audit period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) in coordination with the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) and the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism, which jointly enforce Colombia's Regime of International Foreign Exchange (Mercado Cambiario).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) operates within a managed floating exchange-rate regime. Current account transactions, including cross-border legal services, are freely convertible through the authorized foreign-exchange market, subject to documentary declarations and the availability of Form 52 (Declaración de Cambio). Capital account transactions are restricted only by registration and reporting gates: foreign direct investment into a Colombian S.A.S. must be registered with Banco de la República through the receiving local bank to secure subsequent dividend repatriation and capital-reduction remittances. Profits and dividends are remittable abroad after local tax settlement and presentation of the corresponding foreign-exchange declaration. There is no statutory quantitative limit on profit remittance, but the repatriation must match the net after-tax amount and be supported by an annual shareholders' meeting resolution and DIAN tax-attestation where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For services exports such as cross-border litigation and arbitration fees, the foreign currency inflow must be canalizado through a Colombian authorized bank within six months from the date of the invoice, service completion, or collection milestone. Banco de la República's Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83 requires the export proceeds to be fully channeled through the Mercado Cambiario; the mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 100% for services exports unless the exporter has received a specific foreign-currency account authorization to maintain a working balance. Exporters of goods may retain up to 20% of the proceeds in foreign-currency accounts; services exporters generally must negotiate the full collected amount into COP. Late canalización triggers graduated fines and automatic adjustments to the tax cost base.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for direct non-resident EMI onboarding. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer) cannot offer Colombian IOLTA/trust-account capabilities because Colombian regulation reserves deposit-taking of client funds to licensed credit institutions and to Sociedades Especializadas en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos (SEDPEs) supervised by the Financial Superintendence of Colombia. Offshore EMIs may be used only as pre-funding front-end collection rails provided the ultimate settlement lands in a local bank account; they are not a legally compliant custody or escrow vehicle for cross-border litigation proceeds. A medium-viability local workaround is partnering with a certified SEDPE or licensed remittance company that maintains a local nostro/trust ledger.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of the S.A.S. legal representative and one additional director is generally mandatory for the first compliance interview at Colombian Tier-1 banks. Remote video onboarding is permitted only when the company has a local footprint, a Colombian domiciliary address, and clear registros in the Cámara de Comercio; for a fully foreign-owned S.A.S. without local management, banks require a notarized power of attorney to the legal representative and, in most cases, an in-person or video interview with the ultimate beneficial owner. Some banks accept biometric live-video KYC for low-risk corporate clients, but the issuance of a trust/IOLTA-type account still demands a physical visit by the firm's AML compliance officer or a local attorney with power of attorney.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Annual Commercial Registry Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every calendar year from January 1 through March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers fines (up to approximately 1.5% of average monthly net assets), interest, and continued non-renewal may lead to suspension or cancellation of the commercial registry and loss of legal capacity to engage in commerce.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Estados Financieros Anuales (Annual Financial Statements Filing/Deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to timely deposit financial statements prevents issuance of the annual commercial registry renewal and exposes the company to fines and suspension of the commercial registration effectiveness.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Reporte de Beneficiario Final (Annual Beneficial Owner Information Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the date fixed by DIAN resolution (commonly the last business day of the second or third quarter); updated within one month after any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate UBO filing carries fines from approximately COP 1.2 million to COP 80 million (≈USD 300–20,000); does not directly trigger strike-off but creates tax and AML compliance consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between mid-March and mid-May of the following tax year, determined by the last digit of the taxpayer NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of tax due (minimum of 10 UVT) plus daily interest and inflation adjustment; enforced collection actions and potential de-registration of the RUT for prolonged non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Colombian Commercial Code, an S.A.S. must appoint a Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) if gross assets exceed 5,000 monthly minimum wages (approx. COP 6,500,000,000 for 2024) or gross revenues exceed 3,000 monthly minimum wages (approx. COP 3,900,000,000 for 2024). A voluntary audit may also be required by the company's bylaws or by specific regulations applicable to legal service providers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS or IFRS for SMEs as incorporated by Law 1314 of 2009 and Decree 2420 of 2015 (with amendments), depending on entity size and corporate group requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: In each fiscal year, all Colombian legal entities must report to DIAN the ultimate beneficial owners—natural persons who directly or indirectly own or control 5% or more of the shareholding or voting rights, or who otherwise exert control. The annual report must be updated within 30 days of any relevant shareholding transfer or control change; the system-generated confirmation receipt must be preserved in the corporate file.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Libro de Registro de Representantes Legales y Miembros de Junta Directiva, if applicable)
Shareholders' Meeting Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 – 480 per year for a registered agency / virtual office (domiciliación) in Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali, inclusive of basic RUT assistance.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 7,500 for a standard statutory audit under IFRS for an S.A.S. law firm; USD 1,000 – 2,500 if only a limited review or compilation engagement is sufficient.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for commercial litigation chambers. Deductions are allowed for payroll, technology diffusion, and legally admissible cross-border expert costs; a 50% tax credit is available for STI projects approved by MinCiencias. The Colombian law also permits accelerated depreciation and an 80-100% deduction for certain offshore software/IT services, but these do not apply to arbitration/litigation revenue; hence the effective CIT approximates the headline rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 - Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para Personas Jurídicas y Asimiladas; e-filed through DIAN MUISCA (RH&F) electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, due in April (from about 9 to 24 April) determined by the last digit of NIT; non-December year ends are due by the 4th/6th month close, following precision.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: NIT, legal name, and tax-registration regime (Régimen Ordinario).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Colombian S.A.S. NIT; foreign shareholders need not be listed here, but controlling parties must be flagged in the Beneficial Ownership annex (Form 310).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Colombian-source revenue: legal fees, retainers, court-ordered cost awards, arbitration receipts, and any consultancy income under ISIC 6910.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not include funds held in IOLTA trust for clients; they are liabilities. Report only earned fees; cross-border litigation pass-throughs must be netted and evidenced by engagement letters.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating deductions: personnel, premises, expert witnesses, overseas counsel fees, IT and administrative costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support all deductions with electronic invoices/e-mails and contract files; if the counterparty is a related nonresident, cap cost deduction at arm's-length quantum and submit TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable ordinary income after NOL offset: computed as gross revenue minus deductions and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that any previous Colombian NOL offset does not exceed the 12-year window; if the NOL arose from cross-border transactions, re-run transfer-pricing adjustments from source year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable (35% of taxable income after discounts/credits) and complementarios.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where treaty-eligible foreign shareholders receive a dividend, apply 10% dividend WHT. The return must reconcile WHT declarations to avoid an under-payment trigger.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late payment: 5% per month (or fraction) of the tax due, not exceeding 100% of tax; if no tax due, a liquidated penalty ranging from ~COP 250,000 to COP 3,500,000 is imposed. Deficient returns present a 20% under-report penalty and interest at up to 2.4% monthly (Art. 634-635 ET) plus a restrictive regime for exclusion from state contracts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding on dividends paid to non-residents from after-tax Colombian profits; an additional 35% withholding applies to distributions sourced from profits not subject to corporate tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief, the nonresident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (CRF) from its tax authority and submit it through the Colombian withholding agent to DIAN electronically before payment. The withholding agent enters the treaty rate on the DIAN withholding return and attaches the certificate and legal analysis. If relief is denied, a refund may be pursued within 2 years (Art. 254 ET) using judicial channels.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 33%; under applicable DTAs commonly reduced to 10%–15% (e.g., Spain 10%, Chile 15%). Interest: statutory rate 15%; under applicable DTAs commonly reduced to 5%–15%, and interest paid to qualified foreign financial institutions may be reduced to 0%–5% in specific treaty cases.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local and Master File, with Informative Return Form 1206, when the taxpayer's gross assets or gross revenues exceed 100,000 UVT (COP 4,706 million approx. for 2024) and related-party aggregate turnover exceeds 10,000 UVT (COP 470.65 million approx.). DIAN Resolutions change the UVT each year; lower thresholds apply for transactions in free trade zones or with residents of tax havens.
